messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm rolling a small canary to move a subset of pods to the new NAT gateway autoscaling group. Need 👀 on the TF changes that modify route propagation for our interface endpoints (PrivateLink).

maya: PR here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/523 — it's mostly route table and endpoint wiring. Trying to avoid breaking egress from k8s e2e jobs.

maya: Relevant snippet from the plan: 
```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association" "svc_pl_endpoint_rt_assoc" {
  vpc_endpoint_id = aws_vpc_endpoint.svc_pl.id
  route_table_id  = aws_route_table.private_rt.id
}

# switching propagation flag to true on TGW attachment
resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment" "tgw_attach" {
  transit_gateway_id = aws_ec2_transit_gateway.main.id
  vpc_id             = var.vpc_id
  subnet_ids         = var.private_subnet_ids
  options {
    appliance_mode_support = "disable"
    ipv6_support = "disable"
  }
}
```

kevin: On first pass — watch the route table priority. If the interface endpoint adds a route to the private RT, make sure it doesn't shadow the NAT route for 0.0.0.0/0.

kevin: Also cc @samir for the TGW propagation toggle — we had a subtly different setting in prod last quarter to avoid cross-account leaks.

samir: quick note: TGW attachment propagation is separate from the endpoint RT assoc. If you flip propagation to true you can wind up leaking routes into the TGW route table unless you explicitly restrict route table propagation.

samir: For the canary I'd recommend: 1) keep propagation off, 2) add an explicit route for the PL endpoints in the VPC RT, 3) run the canary for 1h, check logs/egress.

maya: Sounds safe. Would you object if I temporarily add a lifecycle ignore_changes on the tgw attachment while we validate?

luis: If you do that please add a clear comment and an issue linking the follow-up. We burnt cycles last time with lingering ignores.

kevin: example to avoid propagation: 
```hcl
resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_association" "tgw_rt_assoc" {
  transit_gateway_attachment_id = aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach.id
  transit_gateway_route_table_id = aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table.main.id
  # deliberately not enabling propagation for canary
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = ["propagation"]
  }
}
```

infra-bot: deploy-check: infra/pr/523 — plan succeeded (3 resources to add, 2 to change). CI tests passed.

maya: Thanks — deploying the canary to us-west-2 now. I'll post metrics in ~30m.

luis: ping me once perf looks stable and I'll review the PR for full rollout.

samir: Also make sure the k8s egress policy has a fallback to the legacy natgw. We had a misroute in staging where a pod lost internet access during endpoint failover.

maya: Good call. Adding a short-lived TF var to keep legacy NAT in the routing chain during the canary.

maya: Update: 30m in — canary health checks green, curl to external services works from canary pods. No changes in error budget.

kevin: Nice. When you flip propagation in the full rollout, remember to run the route-summary script and check TGW tables vs VPC tables.

maya: Will do. Leaving the ignore_changes in for now and creating follow-up issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/789

luis: Awesome. If nothing changes in the next 2h, we can plan a staged rollout across the remaining subnets tomorrow. :thumbsup:
